title.source: 戴森無袋原型，為何還得跨國重做？｜品牌故事
title.text: Dyson's bagless prototype: why rebuild it overseas?｜Brand Story

description.source:
一台無袋原型能試用，為什麼還得跨國重新開發，再回到自家製造與英國接貨？從工廠粉末堵布濾、家用袋孔診斷、紙板與金屬模型試作、授權與日本共同開發，走到模具融資、租用組裝空間、郵購實演與售點說明。

日本之前已有英國獲授權的Cyclon產品，1983–84/550台是戴森回顧；義大利製只限館藏單件，不稱日本為全球第一市場。1985西麻布改吸頭照片、1986與Apex達成授權協議的回憶及日本發售分開，不倒推簽約日。M+1983/Silver Seiko、V&A1986/APEX、科學博物館群1985–1990/Apex是不同館藏欄位，不是同一份首售或製造合約。

新材料採本人訪談原發布頁、公司傳記與Robin Roy訪談研究。Masters of Scale官方逐字稿明示自動產生且未全校正，作者未另聽音檔；相關細節仍待獨立來源審查。新銀行回憶與舊Fortune日期/幣別口徑不同，旁白只採內部爭取與房屋擔保，不拼成精確年額。租半廠的訪談沒有地點日期，不能等同1993 Bumpers Farm；乾粉示範先撒配套粉後吸除，不是濕吸證明或通用效能測試。廣告與訂單交換為另一段未定年的初期英國通路回憶，不能指定為首家郵購買手同一交易。

description.text:
If a bagless prototype already worked, why redevelop it overseas, then return to in-house manufacturing and early British retail orders? Follow factory powder clogging a cloth filter, the diagnosis of a household bag's pores, cardboard and metal prototypes, licensing and joint Japanese development, then tooling finance, rented assembly space, mail-order demonstrations and in-store explanations.

A licensed British Cyclon product existed before Japan; 1983–84 and 550 units come from Dyson's recollection. Italian manufacture applies only to the museum's individual object. Japan is not described as the first market worldwide. The 1985 Nishi-Azabu head-redesign photo, the recalled 1986 agreement with Apex and the Japanese launch are separate records, not grounds for backdating a contract. M+'s 1983/Silver Seiko, V&A's 1986/APEX and the Science Museum Group's 1985–1990/Apex are different collection fields, not one record of a first sale or manufacturing contract.

New material comes from original interview publication pages, the company biography and Robin Roy's interview research. Masters of Scale labels its official transcript as automatically generated and not fully corrected; the author has not separately listened to the audio, and the relevant details still await independent source review. The new bank recollection differs from the older Fortune account in dates and currencies, so the narration uses only the internal appeal and house collateral, without combining them into a precise year and amount. The half-factory interview supplies no location or date and cannot be equated with Bumpers Farm in 1993. The dry-powder demonstration applies the accompanying powder before vacuuming; it is not evidence of wet pickup or a general performance test. The advertising-for-orders deal is another undated recollection of early British distribution and cannot be identified as the same transaction with the first mail-order buyer.

2566: 他還得面對另一個疑問：目錄裡已有知名品牌，
為什麼要換成這台陌生產品？
zmbc: 戴森回憶，問到工業氣旋的報價，
他們負擔不起，於是花幾個週末自行製作。
dkhw: 你大概也會懷疑，問題真在袋子裝滿嗎？
我想再問，倒空後，袋裡還留著什麼？
y5py: 他用紙板和膠帶做了小氣旋，再用一段軟管，
接到原來的直立式吸塵器上。
3b3d: 可能變好，也可能變差；看懂這次發生什麼，
才決定下一個模型要怎麼做。
5uh4: 我覺得關鍵在這裡：模型不是擺在架上算數，
而是拿來排除一個不知道的地方。
shcn: 戴森把生產列在一九八三、八四年，
並說一共只做五百五十台，商業上沒有成功。
iund: 山本自己的工作室履歷，把加入Apex列在一九八五年，
參與英國團隊的共同開發。
3tsc: 我覺得，接下來的難處是讓這些人的手接上，
不是把樣品交出去就等交貨。
88z5: 是加在氣流進入錐體的入口，避免雜物堵在那裡。
n6tt: 山本說，他們試驗不同大小、不同形狀的孔，
靠這些實驗解決那個入口的堵塞問題。
a57z: 你改完這一端，另一端還得接著做；
我看到的，是一份要反覆往返的工作。
jyqr: 開場問的模具款，戴森回憶，
一位到企業訪問的銀行人員，替他爭取貸款。
4e3p: 他說，對方的請求先被銀行拒絕，
又去找銀行內部的申訴角色，爭取批准。
6w42: 如果換成你，要押上住的房子，
我會先看清楚，哪一筆風險落在自己身上。
3kk2: 開場那四個人，從成型供應商那裡找到一個機會：
對方的工廠，有半邊閒著。
dahx: 租下的半廠在哪裡，那段訪談沒有交代，
不能把兩份記錄當成同一間廠房。
zi48: 戴森記得，面對一名郵購目錄買手時，
對方先懷疑配套的乾粉地毯清潔法。
3qra: 換成你要騰出目錄的位置，
我想你也不會只問能不能吸，還會問能不能賣。
f7dw: 在另一段口述裡，戴森記下，
後來又有第二家郵購目錄，再接到約翰路易斯百貨。
jtzs: 英國智慧財產局的一份決定書，記下他說，
不少潛在零售商不喜歡透明集塵筒。
cvp5: 談英國初期通路的另一段回憶裡，
戴森說，曾有電器零售商要求廣告支持。
6xye: 我對開場問題的答案是：無袋原型解了一段堵塞，
交到顧客手上，還得有人接完製造和接貨的工作。

lines.source: 你只靠四個工程人員，要把新吸塵器交出去，誰來組裝？
lines.text: With just four engineers, who would assemble the new vacuum you needed to deliver?

lines.source: 九〇年代初，戴森決定自己製造。
lines.text: In the early nineties, Dyson decided to manufacture it himself.

lines.source: 他回憶，自己和三名工程師，替全部零件畫圖，再去找承包商和模具商。
lines.text: He recalls drawing every component with three engineers, then looking for contractors and toolmakers.

lines.source: 可是，組裝這一步，他們沒找到人承接。
lines.text: But they found nobody willing to take on the assembly.

lines.source: 我想知道，山本手上那個孔罩，之前又是為哪個入口的麻煩做的？
lines.text: I want to know: which troublesome inlet was that perforated cover in Yamamoto's hands originally made for?

lines.source: 而量產模具的錢，又得由誰去向銀行爭取？
lines.text: And who would persuade a bank to fund the production tooling?

lines.source: 今天跟著戴森，走完一台無袋原型到英國初期接貨的路。
lines.text: Today, follow Dyson from a bagless prototype to its early acceptance by British retailers.

lines.source: 不用集塵袋的想法，中間還要換過多少人的手，才能做成能賣的機器？
lines.text: How many people's hands would the bagless idea have to pass through before it became a machine you could sell?

lines.source: 開場那台無袋吸塵器的原理，是從戴森處理的一個工廠故障接過來的。
lines.text: The principle behind the bagless vacuum in our opening came from a factory problem Dyson had tackled.

lines.source: 公司官網把時間記在一九七八年：他在工廠替金屬架噴粉。
lines.text: The company website dates it to 1978: he was powder-coating metal frames at a factory.

lines.source: 很多粉末沒有留在架子上，抽走餘粉時，又把後面的一大片布濾堵住。
lines.text: Much of the powder missed the frames, and extracting the excess clogged a large cloth filter behind them.

lines.source: 換成你要讓生產繼續，我也會問：要把粉末收住，該換哪一種裝置？
lines.text: If you needed to keep production running, I'd ask the same thing: what other device could collect that powder?

lines.source: 官網還記下，他去看過木材廠的大型氣旋，想把那種分離方式用回工廠。
lines.text: The website also says he saw a large cyclone at a sawmill and wanted to use that separation method at his factory.

lines.source: 戴森回憶，問到工業氣旋的報價，他們負擔不起，於是花幾個週末自行製作。
lines.text: Dyson recalls that an industrial cyclone cost more than they could afford, so they spent several weekends making one themselves.

lines.source: 他說，做出的裝置很大，頂端構造要穿出屋頂，還得在廠房開孔。
lines.text: He says it was so large that its top had to pass through the roof, requiring a hole in the factory building.

lines.source: 這一次，粉末先從空氣裡分離，不再全靠那片布接住。
lines.text: This time, the powder was separated from the air first, rather than relying entirely on the cloth to catch it.

lines.source: 我在意的不是它有多高，而是堵住的地方，讓人換了一種收集辦法。
lines.text: What interests me isn't its height, but how a blockage led them to a different way of collecting powder.

lines.source: 那麼，這個辦法，能不能縮進你家裡那台吸塵器？
lines.text: Could that method be made small enough for the vacuum in your home?

lines.source: 戴森說，有一次在家清掃，機器顯示集塵袋堵了，他卻找不到替換袋。
lines.text: Dyson says that once, while cleaning at home, the machine indicated a blocked bag, but he had no replacement.

lines.source: 於是他把袋子倒空，用膠帶封回去，再裝上試。
lines.text: So he emptied the bag, taped it shut again and refitted it for a try.

lines.source: 袋子裡沒東西了，機器還是吸不動。
lines.text: There was nothing left in the bag, but the machine still wouldn't pick up dirt.

lines.source: 你大概也會懷疑，問題真在袋子裝滿嗎？我想再問，倒空後，袋裡還留著什麼？
lines.text: You might wonder whether a full bag was really the problem. I'd ask what remained after it was emptied.

lines.source: 他重新打開袋子，看見內壁覆著一層細灰。
lines.text: He opened it again and saw a coating of fine dust on the inside.

lines.source: 依他的解釋，空氣必須穿過袋上的氣孔，細灰卻把這些出口堵住了。
lines.text: As he explains it, air had to pass through the bag's pores, but fine dust had blocked those exits.

lines.source: 他買了新袋換上，吸力短暫恢復，之後又往下掉。
lines.text: He bought and fitted a new bag; suction briefly returned, then dropped again.

lines.source: 前面工廠用氣旋收粉，他在家先做什麼，才能試同一個想法？
lines.text: Earlier, a cyclone had collected powder at the factory. What did he first do at home to test the same idea?

lines.source: 他用紙板和膠帶做了小氣旋，再用一段軟管，接到原來的直立式吸塵器上。
lines.text: He made a small cyclone from cardboard and tape, then connected it to his existing upright vacuum with a hose.

lines.source: 原本放袋子的地方，換成這個小模型，他推著機器試用。
lines.text: He replaced the bag with this little model and pushed the machine around to try it.

lines.source: 這只是把分離方式接上舊機驗證，離能賣的完整產品，還有別的工作。
lines.text: That only tested the separation method on an old machine; a complete, saleable product still needed other work.

lines.source: 要繼續改形狀，沒錢買大型機床，模型又怎麼做？
lines.text: Without money for large machine tools, how could he make models to keep changing the shape?

lines.source: 戴森回憶，自己在家工作，買不起車床等設備，就用小工具動手。
lines.text: Dyson recalls working at home: unable to afford equipment like a lathe, he used small tools.

lines.source: 他從舊物店找到金屬滾輪，把材料滾成倒錐形，再焊接起來。
lines.text: He found metal rollers in a second-hand shop, rolled the material into an inverted cone and welded it together.

lines.source: 工具讓他能把下一個形狀做成實物，拿去試，然後再決定怎麼改。
lines.text: The tools let him turn the next shape into something real, test it and then decide what to change.

lines.source: 但如果一次改了好幾處，你怎麼知道，哪一項真的有用？
lines.text: But if you change several things at once, how do you know which change actually helped?

lines.source: 他在另一段訪談裡解釋，試作時一次只改一項，等著看差異。
lines.text: In another interview, he explains that he changed one thing at a time during prototyping and waited to see the difference.

lines.source: 可能變好，也可能變差；看懂這次發生什麼，才決定下一個模型要怎麼做。
lines.text: It might improve or worsen; understanding what happened would determine the next model.

lines.source: 開放大學的訪談研究，也記錄了他製作、測試黃銅、鋁與透明塑料模型。
lines.text: An Open University interview study also records him making and testing models in brass, aluminium and clear plastic.

lines.source: 我覺得關鍵在這裡：模型不是擺在架上算數，而是拿來排除一個不知道的地方。
lines.text: I think that's the key: a model isn't finished just because it's on a shelf. It's a way to resolve an unknown.

lines.source: 能做出工作樣機以後，誰來付模具的錢、把它批量做出來？
lines.text: Once a working prototype existed, who would pay for tooling and make it in quantity?

lines.source: 戴森回憶，他和合作夥伴原先選擇，把工作放在發明、工程與樣機上。
lines.text: Dyson recalls that he and his partner initially chose to focus on invention, engineering and prototypes.

lines.source: 兩人都做過製造，這次希望由取得授權的廠商接下生產。
lines.text: Both had manufacturing experience, but this time they wanted a licensed manufacturer to handle production.

lines.source: 那份訪談研究也指出，這種吸塵器的模具支出，是商品化要跨過的一關。
lines.text: That interview study also identifies tooling expenditure as a hurdle to commercialising this vacuum.

lines.source: 真的有人接下授權，把後面的生產做出來了嗎？
lines.text: Did anyone actually take a licence and carry out the production?

lines.source: 後來，英國一家取得授權的廠商，確實做出Cyclon。
lines.text: A licensed British manufacturer did later make the Cyclon.

lines.source: 戴森把生產列在一九八三、八四年，並說一共只做五百五十台，商業上沒有成功。
lines.text: Dyson dates its production to 1983 and 1984, saying only 550 were made and it was not a commercial success.

lines.source: 科學博物館群所藏的一台，標明在義大利製造，為英國的授權商生產。
lines.text: One example held by the Science Museum Group is labelled as made in Italy for the British licensee.

lines.source: 日本之前已經有商品；Apex這次，又是怎麼找到戴森的？
lines.text: So there was a product before Japan. How did Apex find Dyson this time?

lines.source: 在這段時期，日本Apex社長看見一本設計書上的照片，便聯絡戴森。
lines.text: During this period, the president of Japan's Apex saw a photograph in a design book and contacted Dyson.

lines.source: 山本秀夫在後來的贊助訪談裡說，那是美國一九八四年出版的書。
lines.text: In a later sponsored interview, Yamamoto says it was a book published in the United States in 1984.

lines.source: 戴森帶著一台樣品來到日本，社長原想進口成品，拿到的卻尚未完成。
lines.text: Dyson brought a sample to Japan. The president had wanted to import a finished product, but it wasn't finished.

lines.source: 換成你要進貨，我想你也會問：現在接的是產品，還是一筆開發工作？
lines.text: If you were ordering stock, I imagine you'd ask too: are we taking on a product, or a development project?

lines.source: 在山本的敘述裡，談判改成在日本重新製作，再由戴森交出當地銷售權。
lines.text: In Yamamoto's account, negotiations shifted to remaking it in Japan, with Dyson granting the local sales rights.

lines.source: 山本說，Apex本業是進口文具，沒有自家的工程師和工廠。
lines.text: Yamamoto says Apex imported stationery and had neither its own engineers nor a factory.

lines.source: 社長負責設法找工廠，開發工作，則交給剛轉職的山本。
lines.text: The president set about finding a factory, while development went to Yamamoto, who had just changed jobs.

lines.source: 山本自己的工作室履歷，把加入Apex列在一九八五年，參與英國團隊的共同開發。
lines.text: His studio biography dates his joining Apex to 1985, working on joint development with the British team.

lines.source: 工廠找到了，現場就有人做過這種吸塵器嗎？
lines.text: They found a factory, but had anyone there made this kind of vacuum before?

lines.source: 依山本回憶，承製者原本做精密機械，並不專門做吸塵器。
lines.text: Yamamoto recalls that the manufacturer made precision machinery, rather than specialising in vacuums.

lines.source: 他自己以前，也沒有設計吸塵器的經驗。
lines.text: He himself had never designed a vacuum before, either.

lines.source: 我覺得，接下來的難處是讓這些人的手接上，不是把樣品交出去就等交貨。
lines.text: I think the next challenge was getting these people's work to connect, rather than handing over a sample and waiting for delivery.

lines.source: 你如果想直接沿用原設計，哪個規格差異會先讓人停下來？
lines.text: If you tried to keep the original design, which difference in specifications would stop you first?

lines.source: 山本說，英國和日本的電壓不同，他們得重新找馬達。
lines.text: Yamamoto says different British and Japanese voltages meant they had to find another motor.

lines.source: 要找一百伏特、輸出相近的馬達，結果尺寸比原先大。
lines.text: They needed a 100-volt motor with similar output, but the one they found was larger.

lines.source: 為了把它裝進去，外殼配置也必須重新檢視。
lines.text: To fit it in, they also had to reconsider the casing layout.

lines.source: 如果我是接案的人，會先問：這樣重做，多久才有第一台能試的機器？
lines.text: If I were taking on the project, I'd first ask how long this redesign would take to produce a machine we could test.

lines.source: 依山本多年後的粗略估計，第一台日本試作品，大約花了半年。
lines.text: In a rough estimate made many years later, Yamamoto put the first Japanese prototype at about six months.

lines.source: 可是，裝得起來，放到地毯上推，又會發生什麼事？
lines.text: But once it was assembled, what happened when they pushed it across a carpet?

lines.source: 他回憶，那個馬達很重。
lines.text: He recalls that the motor was very heavy.

lines.source: 機器會吸住地毯，難以前進。
lines.text: The machine sucked itself against the carpet and was hard to move forward.

lines.source: 硬往前推，還曾把輪子推裂。
lines.text: Forcing it forward even cracked the wheels on one occasion.

lines.source: 你大概想問，除了移動，試作還出了哪些狀況？
lines.text: You might ask what other problems appeared in testing, besides movement.

lines.source: 他也提到雜物堵塞、馬達過熱，甚至使外殼熔損的狀況。
lines.text: He also mentions debris blockages and motor overheating, including cases in which the casing melted.

lines.source: 他估計，第一台試作之後，另有約一年半，都在處理陸續出現的問題。
lines.text: He estimates that after the first prototype, another year and a half went into fixing problems as they arose.

lines.source: 山本還指出槽內一個入口，那裡有他參與設計的部件。
lines.text: Yamamoto also points to an inlet inside the bin, with a component he helped design.

lines.source: 這個入口，是把外圍的氣流帶往哪裡？
lines.text: Where did this inlet take the air flowing around the outside?

lines.source: 他描述的路徑，是氣流沿著槽外圍轉，再進到內側的錐體。
lines.text: He describes air swirling around the bin's perimeter, then passing into the cone inside.

lines.source: 開場那個孔罩，山本說，是加在氣流進入錐體的入口，避免雜物堵在那裡。
lines.text: Yamamoto says the perforated cover from our opening was fitted at the cone's air inlet to keep debris from blocking it.

lines.source: 要讓雜物繼續在外圍轉動，空氣則經過入口往內走。
lines.text: Debris needed to keep circulating outside, while air passed through the inlet towards the centre.

lines.source: 加了這個部件，接著要調整的是什麼？
lines.text: Once this component was added, what needed adjusting next?

lines.source: 山本說，他們試驗不同大小、不同形狀的孔，靠這些實驗解決那個入口的堵塞問題。
lines.text: Yamamoto says they tested different hole sizes and shapes, using those experiments to solve the inlet blockage.

lines.source: 孔要改，另一端設計的人，也得知道日本這邊試到了哪裡。
lines.text: As the holes changed, the designer at the other end also needed to know how the Japanese tests were progressing.

lines.source: 戴森回英國時，這些設計要怎麼繼續接下去？
lines.text: When Dyson returned to Britain, how could that design work continue?

lines.source: 山本說，戴森人在英國時，他們就一再傳真往返。
lines.text: Yamamoto says that when Dyson was in Britain, they repeatedly exchanged faxes.

lines.source: 訪談展示的圖紙和傳真頁，還留下這些合作文件。
lines.text: Drawings and fax pages shown in the interview preserve records of that collaboration.

lines.source: 你改完這一端，另一端還得接著做；我看到的，是一份要反覆往返的工作。
lines.text: You change something at this end, and the other end must follow up. What I see is work going back and forth.

lines.source: 圖面要完成，問題也要有人接手，約定裡由誰負責？
lines.text: The drawings had to be finished and problems dealt with. Who was responsible under their agreement?

lines.source: 依山本回憶，戴森負有解決問題、完成圖面的責任。
lines.text: Yamamoto recalls that Dyson was responsible for solving problems and completing the drawings.

lines.source: 除了傳真，他本人有沒有到日本一起做？
lines.text: Besides faxing, did he come to Japan to work alongside them?

lines.source: 山本說，為了走到能販售的階段，戴森曾數度來日本。
lines.text: Yamamoto says Dyson visited Japan several times to get the machine ready for sale.

lines.source: 每次停留，大約是一到兩週。
lines.text: Each stay lasted roughly one or two weeks.

lines.source: 兩人一起到工廠、畫圖，也一起做實驗。
lines.text: They went to the factory, drew designs and carried out experiments together.

lines.source: 你想看他具體動手改什麼，一張官網照片，留下了哪個工作？
lines.text: If you want to see what he actually changed, what work does a photograph on the company website preserve?

lines.source: 圖說記為一九八五年東京西麻布，正在重設後來G-Force的吸頭。
lines.text: Its caption places him in Nishi-Azabu, Tokyo, in 1985, redesigning the head of what became the G-Force.

lines.source: 戴森在後來口述裡，把與Apex達成授權協議放在一九八六年。
lines.text: In a later oral account, Dyson dates the licence agreement with Apex to 1986.

lines.source: 這和前一年的改圖，是不同記錄，不能併成一個精確簽約日。
lines.text: That and the previous year's redesign are separate records, not a precise contract date we can combine them into.

lines.source: 山本訪談把日本G-Force的發售，也記在一九八六年。
lines.text: Yamamoto's interview also dates the Japanese G-Force launch to 1986.

lines.source: 你會以為能上架就會大賣嗎？我想問，這回究竟是多大一門生意？
lines.text: Would you expect reaching the shelves to mean huge sales? I want to know how big this business really was.

lines.source: 戴森在二〇一七年的口述裡，稱它是小眾商品，每台約二十五萬日圓。
lines.text: In his 2017 oral account, Dyson calls it a niche product, priced at around 250,000 yen each.

lines.source: 他說，Apex賣這台機器，沒有取得很大的商業成功。
lines.text: He says Apex did not achieve great commercial success with the machine.

lines.source: 但授權合作，確實開始替他帶來收入。
lines.text: But the licensing partnership did begin bringing him income.

lines.source: 要走到開場那批零件圖，還差自家製造需要的資金和場地。
lines.text: To reach those component drawings from our opening, he still needed funding and premises for his own manufacturing.

lines.source: 收入進來了，量產模具的錢，就一定借得到嗎？
lines.text: Once income was coming in, was borrowing for production tooling guaranteed?

lines.source: 開場問的模具款，戴森回憶，一位到企業訪問的銀行人員，替他爭取貸款。
lines.text: For the tooling funds we asked about at the start, Dyson recalls a visiting bank employee who argued for a loan on his behalf.

lines.source: 他說，對方的請求先被銀行拒絕，又去找銀行內部的申訴角色，爭取批准。
lines.text: He says the bank first rejected that employee's request, so the employee approached an internal appeals role to seek approval.

lines.source: 他自己拿房屋作擔保，太太也得在相關表格上簽名。
lines.text: Dyson put his house up as security, and his wife also had to sign the relevant forms.

lines.source: 如果換成你，要押上住的房子，我會先看清楚，哪一筆風險落在自己身上。
lines.text: If you had to pledge the house you lived in, I'd first want to understand which risks fell on me.

lines.source: 錢能買模具，開場卻還缺組裝的人；這件事，要先找到哪一個落腳處？
lines.text: Money could buy tooling, but the opening still lacked assemblers. Where would they first find a place to work?

lines.source: 開場那四個人，從成型供應商那裡找到一個機會：對方的工廠，有半邊閒著。
lines.text: Those four people found an opportunity with a moulding supplier: half its factory was standing idle.

lines.source: 他提出把閒置的半邊租下來，用來組裝，就不必先買一整座廠房。
lines.text: He proposed renting that unused half for assembly, avoiding the need to buy an entire factory first.

lines.source: 但模具仍得自己投資，租到空間，沒有把這筆支出一起省掉。
lines.text: But they still had to invest in tooling; renting space didn't remove that expense.

lines.source: 那麼，空間有了，誰安排組裝線，誰實際上線做？
lines.text: With space secured, who would organise the assembly line, and who would work on it?

lines.source: 他回憶，最初沒有另外設置生產經理和品管專員，只有那個工程團隊。
lines.text: He recalls that initially there was no separate production manager or quality-control specialist, just the engineering team.

lines.source: 開場問的組裝，最後還得另外聘線長，再聘真正上線組裝的工人。
lines.text: The assembly question from the opening finally required hiring a line leader and workers to do the actual assembly.

lines.source: 公司另有一張標作一九九三年的產線照，留下的是哪個現場？
lines.text: The company also has a production-line photograph dated 1993. Which site does it show?

lines.source: 那張照片的地點，是英國奇彭納姆的邦帕斯農場。
lines.text: That photograph was taken at Bumpers Farm in Chippenham, Britain.

lines.source: 多台機器排在線上，有人在工作，旁邊也有紙箱。
lines.text: Several machines stand along a line, with people working and boxes nearby.

lines.source: 租下的半廠在哪裡，那段訪談沒有交代，不能把兩份記錄當成同一間廠房。
lines.text: The interview doesn't locate the rented half-factory, so we cannot treat these two records as the same premises.

lines.source: 可是，有了能交的機器，你就一定找得到店家接貨嗎？
lines.text: But even with machines ready to deliver, were you certain to find retailers willing to stock them?

lines.source: 戴森記得，面對一名郵購目錄買手時，對方先懷疑配套的乾粉地毯清潔法。
lines.text: Dyson remembers a mail-order catalogue buyer first doubting the accompanying dry-powder carpet-cleaning method.

lines.source: 他去加油站買黑醋栗飲料，回來倒在地毯上，再撒上乾洗粉。
lines.text: He bought a blackcurrant drink at a petrol station, poured it onto the carpet and then sprinkled on dry-cleaning powder.

lines.source: 然後才用機器吸除。依他的回憶，這場示範成功了。
lines.text: Only then did he vacuum it up. In his recollection, the demonstration worked.

lines.source: 要看清楚，他示範的是先用配套乾洗粉，不是宣稱機器能直接濕吸飲料。
lines.text: To be clear, he used the accompanying cleaning powder first; this wasn't a claim that the machine could directly wet-vacuum the drink.

lines.source: 可買手看完，為什麼仍然沒有立刻點頭？
lines.text: But why didn't the buyer agree immediately after watching?

lines.source: 他還得面對另一個疑問：目錄裡已有知名品牌，為什麼要換成這台陌生產品？
lines.text: He still faced another question: with famous brands already in the catalogue, why replace them with this unfamiliar product?

lines.source: 他回憶，買手最後答應先試一試，成了第一家備貨的郵購目錄。
lines.text: He recalls that the buyer finally agreed to give it a try, becoming the first mail-order catalogue to stock it.

lines.source: 換成你要騰出目錄的位置，我想你也不會只問能不能吸，還會問能不能賣。
lines.text: If you were making room in your catalogue, I imagine you'd ask not only whether it could clean, but whether it could sell.

lines.source: 在另一段口述裡，戴森記下，後來又有第二家郵購目錄，再接到約翰路易斯百貨。
lines.text: In another oral account, Dyson says a second mail-order catalogue followed, and then John Lewis.

lines.source: 走進店面以後，使用者能看見的灰塵，店家又願不願意展示？
lines.text: Once it reached shops, would retailers also be willing to display the dust users could see?

lines.source: 英國智慧財產局的一份決定書，記下他說，不少潛在零售商不喜歡透明集塵筒。
lines.text: A UK Intellectual Property Office decision records him saying that many potential retailers disliked the clear bin.

lines.source: 但他認為，顧客能看見灰塵的位置、理解運作，也能看見清掃的效果。
lines.text: But he believed customers could see where the dust was, understand how it worked and see the cleaning results.

lines.source: 依這份證詞，他仍選擇保留透明設計。
lines.text: According to that testimony, he still chose to keep the transparent design.

lines.source: 我想，買手聽過一次示範，店裡的你卻未必聽過；誰來把差別說清楚？
lines.text: I think the buyer had seen a demonstration, but you, standing in the shop, might not have. Who would explain the difference?

lines.source: 戴森回憶，他得爭取零售商同意，在機器旁擺上技術和差異的說明資料。
lines.text: Dyson recalls having to persuade retailers to put information about the technology and its differences beside the machine.

lines.source: 他想讓買家不只比較折扣和價格，也看性能、耐用和使用方式。
lines.text: He wanted buyers to consider performance, durability and use, as well as discounts and prices.

lines.source: 但如果通路還要求廣告支持，手邊又沒有現成預算，條件怎麼談？
lines.text: But if a retailer also wanted advertising support and there was no ready budget, how could they negotiate?

lines.source: 談英國初期通路的另一段回憶裡，戴森說，曾有電器零售商要求廣告支持。
lines.text: In another recollection of early British retailing, Dyson says an electrical retailer once requested advertising support.

lines.source: 他當時沒錢做廣告，便提議按店家的訂購量，投入約定的電視廣告。
lines.text: Without money for advertising at the time, he proposed agreed television advertising tied to the retailer's order volume.

lines.source: 戴森說，雙方是按這個條件達成交易。
lines.text: Dyson says they reached a deal on those terms.

lines.source: 我對開場問題的答案是：無袋原型解了一段堵塞，交到顧客手上，還得有人接完製造和接貨的工作。
lines.text: My answer to our opening question is this: the bagless prototype solved part of a blockage problem, but manufacturing and getting retailers to take it still needed people to finish the work.

lines.source: 如果換成你接案，哪一步沒完成，你就不敢把產品交出去？留言告訴我。
lines.text: If you took on this project, which unfinished step would stop you from handing the product over? Tell me in the comments.

lines.source: 想看日用品怎麼跨過這些實際難關，就訂閱品牌故事。
lines.text: Subscribe to Brand Story to see how everyday products overcome practical obstacles like these.
